SUBCONTRACTOR AGREEMENT
This Subcontractor Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into as of the date set forth on the signature page (“Effective Date”), by and between McClintock Electric Inc. (“Contractor”) and the undersigned subcontractor (“Subcontractor”).
1. SCOPE OF WORK. As used herein, the “Project” is as more fully described on Exhibit A attached hereto and made part hereof. The scope of the Project may be amended by the mutual consent of the parties by a work order, statement of work, order form, or other ordering document (each, a “Statement of Work”). A Statement of Work may be placed by email and accepted by an email confirmation receipt. Each Statement of Work is subject to the terms of, and is deemed incorporated into, this Agreement and is effective beginning on the date set forth thereon. Subcontractor agrees to follow all reasonable rules, regulations, and codes of conduct of Contractor, as Contractor may determine from time to time.
2. PRIME CONTRACT. Subcontractor shall be bound to Contractor by the terms of this Agreement and of the contract documents between Contractor and the customer (“Prime Contract”), and shall assume toward Contractor all the obligations and responsibilities which Contractor, by those documents, assumes toward the customer, insofar as applicable to this Agreement, provided that where any provision of the contract documents between Contractor and the customer is inconsistent with any provision of this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern.
3. APPROVAL BY CUSTOMER. If the customer cancels the Prime Contract, suspends work thereunder or eliminates a portion of the work, the rights of Subcontractor in reference to work already done hereunder shall be the same as the rights of Contractor against the customer under the Prime Contract, except that the amounts, if any, to be paid by Contractor to Subcontractor shall be computed on the basis of the prices used in arriving at the price of this Agreement as determined under Section 4 of this Agreement; provided, however, Contractor shall in no event be required to pay Subcontractor more than Contractor receives from the customer for the work done pursuant to this Agreement.
4. PRICE. As full compensation for the performance of this Agreement, Contractor shall pay Subcontractor the amount set forth on Exhibit A, subject to additions and deductions as provided for in this Agreement. Subcontractor shall comply with Federal, State, and local tax laws, social security acts, unemployment compensation acts and workers’ compensation acts related to the performance of this Agreement.
5. PAYMENT. Payment shall be due to Subcontractor within five (5) days after: (i) the work and materials set forth in this Agreement are fully completed and performed in accordance with Contractor’s requirements; and (ii) Contractor has received from the customer payment in full. If the customer has failed for whatever reason to issue full payment to Contractor, Contractor – under no circumstances – is responsible to Subcontractor for such unpaid sums until paid by customer. The parties to this Agreement specifically acknowledge and agree that a condition precedent to the obligation of Contractor to pay Subcontractor is the payment to Contractor by the customer; this provision does not merely set forth the time at which payment must be made to Subcontractor. Subcontractor acknowledges that this is a “pay-if-paid” provision, that the risk of the customer’s non-payment is being shifted from Contractor to Subcontractor, and that Subcontractor may not be paid if the customer fails to pay Contractor for work performed and/or materials provided by Subcontractor. Notwithstanding any provisions to the contrary, Contractor may withhold payments from Subcontractor (whether or not Contractor has been paid by customer) where Contractor, the architect/engineer, or customer discovers evidence, makes observations, or has determined that any of the following events may exist or have occurred: (a) Subcontractor has failed to timely remedy its defective work or defective materials; (b) third-party claims have been or may be filed against the customer, Contractor, architect/engineer or Project arising out of actions or transactions attributable to Subcontractor; (c) Subcontractor failed to make prompt payment to other subcontractors, laborers, or materialmen; (d) Subcontractor’s work is delayed such that the Project will not be substantially or finally complete within the time specified in the Prime Contract; or (e) Contractor may be subject to liquidated damages or actual damages as a result of anticipated delays or other events caused either in whole or in part by Subcontractor.
In cases where Contractor, in its sole discretion, has determined that any of the foregoing events may exist or have occurred, Contractor, in addition to any other remedies, may deduct any damages, costs and expenses incurred as a result of or in any way associated with the existence or occurrence of such event(s) from any money then due or thereafter to become due to Subcontractor, including but not limited to Contractor’s attorney’s fees.
6. TIME OF COMMENCEMENT AND COMPLETION. Time is of the essence for all aspects of the Agreement. No extension of time will be valid without Contractor’s written consent after timely claim made by Subcontractor in accordance with this Agreement. If Subcontractor defaults on any portion of the work outlined in this Agreement, Contractor reserves the right to employ others to satisfactorily complete this portion of the work and deduct the cost for so doing from the price of this Agreement as set forth in Section 4 of this Agreement and to seek any other damages, costs or expenses incurred.
7. CLAIMS. Subcontractor shall make all claims to Contractor for additional work, extensions of time, and damage for delays or otherwise: in writing and within five (5) days of the occurrence of the event giving rise to such claim. The failure to notify Contractor as provided above shall constitute a waiver of Subcontractor’s right to any damages, additional compensation or extensions of time.
8. CONFIDENTIALITY. Subcontractor acknowledges that during the term of this Agreement, it may be provided with certain proprietary information, including, without limitation prices, data, reports, technical information, trade secrets, know-how, processes, and customer information (“Confidential Information”). Subcontractor agrees that it will not, either during or after the term of this Agreement, for any reason, publish or disclose to any third party, except to its corporate affiliates, without the advance, express written authorization from Contractor, any such Confidential Information of the other party, nor, except to the extent such Confidential Information is necessary in performance of this Agreement, will it use such Confidential Information. Subcontractor will use the same degree of care, but no less than a reasonable degree of care, as the Subcontractor uses with respect to its own similar information to protect the Confidential Information of the Contractor in accordance with this Agreement. The obligations and duties imposed by this Agreement with respect to any Confidential Information may be enforced by Contractor against any and all representatives of Subcontractor to whom such Confidential Information was disclosed or otherwise made available by Subcontractor. The requirements of this Section shall survive for two (2) years after the termination of this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, and upon request of Contractor, all materials and copies of Confidential Information shall be immediately returned to Contractor.
9. NO FURTHER SUBCONTRACTING OR ASSIGNMENT OF AGREEMENT. Subcontractor shall not assign this Agreement or any aspect of the Agreement (other than the acquisition of materials), including any further subcontracting of Subcontractor’s work on the Project, without first obtaining the written approval of Contractor.
10. AUDIT AND ACCESS. Upon reasonable request by Contractor, Subcontractor shall provide any requested records to establish and verify Subcontractor’s compliance with this Agreement and all applicable laws.
11. QUALITY OF WORK. Subcontractor warrants that all work performed and materials furnished under this Agreement shall be of good quality, free from faults and defects and in conformance with the Agreement. All work and materials not conforming to these standards may be considered defective. The warranty provided in this paragraph shall be in addition to and not in limitation of any other warranty or remedy required by law or by the Agreement.
12. FIELD DIMENSIONS. Subcontractor is responsible for taking all appropriate field dimensions to ensure that its materials or construction work are installed satisfactorily on the Project. No request for additional funds will be allowed for items not fitting due to lack of field dimensions.
13. WORKING CONDITIONS. Subcontractor shall be responsible for cleaning up its own debris at all times and in a continuous fashion. In the event Contractor finds it necessary to clean up Subcontractor’s debris, any cleanup expenses incurred by Contractor—or repairs to other areas damaged by Subcontractor—shall be backcharged to Subcontractor and deducted from its final payment. Subcontractor shall verify with Contractor’s job superintendent that cleanup of Subcontractor’s debris is satisfactory.
14. SAFETY. Subcontractor shall take all safety precautions with respect to his work, shall comply with all safety measures initiated by Contractor and with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules, regulations and orders of any public authority for the safety of persons or property in accordance with the requirements of the Agreement. Subcontractor shall report any injury suffered by any of its employees at the site to Contractor within three (3) days of the injury.
15. SAFETY AUDIT. From time to time, at the sole discretion of Contractor, Contractor may perform a safety audit of Subcontractor to ensure that Subcontractor’s compliance with Section 14 of this Agreement and the Contractor’s rules, regulations, and code of conduct related to safety measures and procedures. The criteria for a safety audit shall include, but not be limited to: (i) TRIR; (ii) EMR; (iii) DART; and (iv) any other metric or standard determined to be applicable in the sole discretion of Contractor. If Subcontractor fails to pass Contractor’s safety audit, Contractor and Subcontractor shall within three (3) days of the failed safety audit shall mutually agree upon an acceptable mitigation plan to eliminate non-compliance with Contractor’s safety rules, regulations and code of conduct. If Subcontractor fails to comply with the adopted mitigation plan, Contractor shall have the right to immediately terminate this Agreement.
16. PROGRESS REPORTS. Subcontractor shall furnish periodic progress reports on the work as reasonably requested by Contractor, including information on the status of materials and equipment under this Agreement that may be in the course of preparation or manufacture.
17. COMPLIANCE WITH LAW. Subcontractor shall give all notices and comply with all laws, ordinances, rules, regulations and orders of any public authority bearing on the performance of the work under this Agreement. Subcontractor shall secure and pay for all permits, fees and licenses necessary for the execution of the work described in this Agreement, unless otherwise agreed to by the parties in writing.
18. APPROVAL OF WORK. Subcontractor agrees that all work shall be done subject to the final approval of Contractor. Final approval shall be in the Contractor’s sole discretion. Contractor’s decisions shall be final.
19. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement together with any amendments, exhibits, or Statements of Work shall constitute the entire understanding between the parties with respect to the subject matter contained herein and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties with respect to such subject matter. Neither this Agreement nor any term or provision hereof may be changed or waived orally but only by a signed, written agreement, except as otherwise provided for herein.
20. CHOICE OF LAW. This Agreement and any questions with respect to its construction, interpretation or performance shall be governed by and determined in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio; any dispute regarding this Agreement shall be venued in the Common Pleas Court of Wayne County, Ohio.
21. ASSIGNMENT OF WARRANTIES. Subcontractor assigns to Contractor all of its right, title and interest in and to any and all warranties, express or implied, obtained by Subcontractor from Subcontractor’s lower tier subtrades or suppliers, whether conferred by contract or imposed by law, as a result of work performed and/or materials and equipment furnished to the Project.
22. LIQUIDATED DAMAGES. In the event of a delay in the Project, Subcontractor shall pay liquidated damages to Contractor in an amount equal to the greater of (i) $500 per day or (ii) Subcontractor’s proportional share of the liquidated damages set forth in the Contract. Contractor and Subcontractor, recognizing the inherent difficulty in determining the amount of damages that would be owed in such cases, specifically agree these liquidated damages are not punitive in nature, but are intended as a reasonable estimate of compensation for Contractor’s actual damages arising out of Subcontractor’s delayed completion of the work.
23. INDEMNITY. To the fullest extent permitted by law, Subcontractor shall indemnify, defend (at Subcontractor’s sole expense) and hold harmless Contractor, the customer, affiliated companies of Contractor, their parents, joint ventures, representatives, members, designees, officers, directors, shareholders, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (“Indemnified Parties”), from and against any and all claims for bodily injury, death or damage to property, demands, damages, actions causes of action, suits, losses, judgments, obligations and any liabilities, costs and expenses (including but not limited to investigative and repair costs, attorneys fees and costs and consultant fees and costs) (“Claims”) which arise or are in any way connected with the work performed, materials furnished, or services provided under this Agreement by Subcontractor or its agents. These indemnity and defense obligations shall apply to any acts or omissions, negligent or willful misconduct of Indemnified Parties.
24. ATTORNEYS’ FEES. If Contractor employs an attorney to institute legal action against Subcontractor (or any of its lower tier subtrades) or to enforce any of the provisions of the Agreement or to defend or protect its interests in any matter arising out of this Agreement, then Contractor shall be entitled to recover from Subcontractor, in addition to any other damages, its reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs, charges and expenses incurred therein.
25. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR RELATIONSHIP. The parties hereby acknowledge and agree that Subcontractor is an independent contractor of Contractor. Subcontractor is not an employee or agent of Contractor. This Agreement shall not be construed as one of employment. Subcontractor is solely responsible for, and accepts exclusive liability for, the payment of any taxes, including, without limitation, all federal, state and local income taxes, social security tax, unemployment tax, workers’ compensation, and any other required fees or taxes. Subcontractor will not receive any benefits from Contractor other than the compensation stated herein.

A. Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000 each occurrence, with a $2,000,000 general aggregate on a per project basis. The insurance coverage required shall be of sufficient type, scope, and duration to ensure coverage for the Contractor or customer for liability related to any manifestation date within the applicable statutes of limitation and/or repose which pertain to any work performed by or on behalf of the Contractor or customer in relation to the project.
